ECSS 2024: Relative fat mass is not associated with muscle adaptations to resistance training

Author

Hamarsland, Hammarström

Participants

Training conditions and outcome agreement

Effects of baseline relative fat mass and training condition on Vastus lateralis thickness

Leg lean mass (DXA)

Strength

Sex interactions

Male gain in leg lean mass was 2.6%, [1.4, 3.8] and in females 2.3%, [1.1, 3.4]. The average estimated difference between males and females was 0.3%-points, [-1.4, 2]. The average difference between conditions was -0.2%-point, [-1.2, 0.8] in male and 0.8%-point, [-0.2, 1.7] in females. The differences between sexes condition-differences was estimated to -1%-points, [-2.4, 0.4]. For every percentage-point increase in baseline fat mass, males were estimated to have a 0%-point, [-0.2, 0.3] and females 0%-point, [-0.2, 0.2] difference in leg lean mass training induced change. Difference between sexes was estimated to 0%-points, [-2.4, 0.4].

Male gain in vastus lateralis thickness was 2.6%, [1.4, 3.8] and in females 2.3%, [1.1, 3.4]. The average estimated difference between males and females was 0.3%-points, [-1.4, 2]. The average difference between conditions was 2.7%-point, [-0.3, 5.8] in male and 1.2%-point, [-1.8, 4.2] in females. The differences between sexes condition-differences was estimated to 1.5%-points, [-2.7, 5.8]. For every percentage-point increase in baseline fat mass, males were estimated to have a -0.1%-point, [-0.6, 0.3] and females -0.3%-point, [-0.6, 0.1] difference in vastus lateralis thickness training induced change. Difference between sexes was estimated to 0.1%-points, [-2.7, 5.8].

Male gain in average strength was 2.6%, [1.4, 3.8] and in females 2.3%, [1.1, 3.4]. The average estimated difference between males and females was 0.3%-points, [-1.4, 2]. The average difference between conditions was -4.4%-point, [-6.5, -2.3] in male and -5.6%-point, [-7.6, -3.6] in females. The differences between sexes condition-differences was estimated to 1.2%-points, [-1.7, 4.1]. For every percentage-point increase in baseline fat mass, males were estimated to have a -0.3%-point, [-0.6, 0.1] and females -0.1%-point, [-0.4, 0.2] difference in average strength training induced change. Difference between sexes was estimated to -0.2%-points, [-1.7, 4.1].
